newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Glaverbel sets up Chinese unit.
newsitem.headline: Glaverbel sets up Chinese unit.

text.p: Belgian glass maker Glaverbel SA said on Monday it invested $5 million in a new subsidiary in southern China which will process sheets of extra-thin float glass supplied by the group's plant in Mol, Belgium.
Glaverbel, controlled by Japan's Asahi Glass Co Ltd, said activities at Glaverbel Vertec (Shenzhen) Co in Shenzhen in the Guangdong region -- near Hong Kong -- were due to start later this year.
The new company will employ about 40 people, it said in a statement.

"The setting-up in China of a processing line for high quality extra-thin glass, destined for the liquid crystal display (LCD) market, is in response to the rapid growth in demand in this region over the last two years."

Glaverbel said it had already built up a leading position in the market for soda lime float glass, with thicknesses ranging from 0.4 to 1.1 millimetres, for applications such as calculators, watches, car instrument panels, electronic games and domestic appliances.
The new company will reinforce Glaverbel's position in South East Asia, it said.
